newsitem.title: USA: Ford adds 15,000 trucks to Q2 output plan.
newsitem.headline: Ford adds 15,000 trucks to Q2 output plan.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Wednesday it has added 15,000 trucks to its second quarter production plan, bringing the company's total truck output increase over the year-ago period to 92,000 units, or 13 percent.
Ford also said it added about 5,000 cars to its second quarter production plan compared to estimates released a month ago.

Ford now plans to build about 466,000 cars during the second quarter, about 13.9 percent below the 541,000 it built in the same period of 1996. Ford's total truck output for the quarter now stands at about 772,000, compared to 680,000 in the year-ago period.

Ford spokesman George Pipas said the truck production increase was primarily concentrated in Ford's Windstar minivan line, which registered a 6.6 percent increase for May and is up 6.3 percent for the first five months of 1997.
Ford said its May U.S. light vehicle sales showed an overall decline of 3 percent.
Ford's May light truck sales were up 5.2 percent from the year ago period, but domestic passenger car sales were off 11.8 percent.

The truck sales produced another new record for Ford, fueled largely by sport utility vehicles, especially the new Ford Expedition. Ford said it sold a total of 58,879 sport utility vehicles during the month, up 47 percent over last year. Calendar year-to-date, Ford sport utility sales totaled 259,279 units, up 34 percent from last year.

Ford also plans on July 1 to introduce the new Lincoln Navigator luxury sport utility vehicle, which is based on the Expedition platform. The No. 2 U.S. automaker said it currently has dealer orders for nearly 11,000 Navigators.
Robert Rewey, Ford group vice president of marketing and sales, said industry sales are in line with Ford's expectations, despite softening in the last two months.

"As anticipated, the last couple of months haven't matched the first quarter's sales rate, but year-to-date sales are consistent with our full year forecast -- somewhere in the range of 15 to 15.5 million, about the same as last year," Rewey said in a statement. "The fundamentals in the U.S. economy and our business remain positive -- moderate growth, low inflation, and high employment."
Referring to recent surveys showing consumer confidence near all-time highs, Rewey added, "Apparently, consumers are feeling pretty good about things, too."
